name: Jose Luis Solache Jr.
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Committee on Economic Development, Growth, and Household Impact
district: California State Assembly District 62 (southeast Los Angeles County: Lynwood, South Gate, Paramount, Lakewood, Maywood, Huntington Park, Bellflower, Walnut Park)
years_of_service: December 2, 2024–present. Solache is in his first term; his current term ends December 7, 2026. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary (69.4% of the vote) and is on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot against Republican Paul Irving Jones for a second term.
background: Solache was born in Bellflower, California and grew up in Lynwood, attending local public schools. He earned a B.A. in Liberal Studies from California State University, Dominguez Hills, where he served two terms as Student Body President and as statewide Chair of the California State Student Association. He was elected to the Lynwood Unified School District's Board of Education at age 23, making him one of the youngest elected officials in Los Angeles County at the time; he served three terms on that board, including three terms as Board President, before leaving to serve on the Lynwood City Council. (Source: official Assembly biography, solache.asmdc.org/biography.)

Solache has served as a Councilmember, Mayor Pro Tem, and Mayor of the City of Lynwood since 2013. In that role he worked to recruit job-creating employers to the city, build new parks, expand youth programs, and make City Hall more transparent. (Source: official Assembly biography.)

Solache's path to the Legislature included one earlier defeat: in the March 26, 2019 special primary for California State Senate District 33 (following Ricardo Lara's departure to become Insurance Commissioner), Solache placed fifth in a 12-candidate field with 7.5% of the vote; Lena Gonzalez went on to win the seat. Solache was elected to the Assembly in 2024, placing first in a three-way March 5, 2024 primary with 41.4% against Republican Paul Irving Jones (34.4%) and fellow Democrat Maria Estrada (24.2%), then defeating Jones in the November 5, 2024 general election 66.0% to 34.0%. He assumed office December 2, 2024, becoming Assembly Speaker Anthony Rendon's successor in the seat. (Source: Ballotpedia, Jose Solache.)

voting_record_highlights: AB 466 (2025), requiring public postsecondary institutions to provide students with information about organ, eye, and tissue donation: Solache's first bill to be enacted, sponsored by Donate Life California. Signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on July 28, 2025 as Chapter 60, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text for AB 466, 2025–2026.)

AB 562 (2025), the Placing Foster Youth with Families Act, amending Welfare and Institutions Code Section 309 to strengthen requirements that foster youth be placed with relatives where possible: signed by Gov. Newsom on October 7, 2025 as Chapter 436, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text for AB 562, 2025–2026.)

AB 594 (2025), amending Insurance Code Section 10965.03 to let people no longer enrolled as students withdraw from college/university health insurance plans, sponsored by Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara: signed by Gov. Newsom on October 3, 2025 as Chapter 272, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text for AB 594, 2025–2026.)

AB 1390 (2025), amending Education Code Sections 1090 and 35120 to update monthly compensation levels for school district and county board of education trustees: signed by Gov. Newsom on October 11, 2025 as Chapter 639, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text for AB 1390, 2025–2026.)

SB 42 (2025–2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Solache was one of seven Assembly coauthors. It passed the Assembly 59-20 on September 12, 2025 and was signed by Gov. Newsom on October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Solache was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. Solache has served only the 2025–2026 session to date, so no multi-session attendance comparison is possible even in principle.
